newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bonds sold heavily at close on foreign weakness.
newsitem.headline: NZ bonds sold heavily at close on foreign weakness.

text.p: New Zealand long bonds closed 20 basis points higher in yield on Friday as a "meltdown" in the United States and Australia fed through into the local market.
"A further meltdown sluiced through into New Zealand," said a Wellington trader.
Foreign sellers combined with local selling as a local market left long after Thursday's surprise easing by the Reserve Bank saw yields shoot up as buyers evaporated.
Dealers said selling was less dramatic in the bank bill market but weakness in the currency gave that market a heavy tone and one called it a "dead cat bounce" after Thursday's rally.
"It wasn't a big day, just persistent selling kept it offered all day," he said.
They said the bond market would next week take its lead from the U.S. market which is nervous about tonight's PPI data and the FOMC meeting due on March 25.
"The market is of a mindset to see all markets erode further," said one dealer.
He said it appeared the Reserve Bank was succeeding in getting conditions more to its liking with interest rates higher and the currency lower.
